original_question: Consider a foliation F defined by a fibration with closed basis B and fiber F and π1 (F ) = Zk . Under what hypothesis does any foliation G close to F have a compact leaf close to a fiber?
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s own wording. It correctly targets the general persistence problem for the foliation by fibers of a fibration, includes the condition that the fiber has abelian fundamental group π1 ≅ Z^k, and asks for hypotheses ensuring that every nearby foliation still has a compact leaf near one of the original fibers. This is essentially the exact scope of Question 4.1.
missing_details: The total space of the fibration should be named explicitly: one is considering a fibration π:M→B and the foliation whose leaves are the fibers of π.
The draft uses F both for the foliation and for the fiber; these should be separated to avoid ambiguity.
The phrase "closed basis B" should be standardized to "closed base manifold B".
It should be explicit that the fiber is the compact leaf type under discussion; writing the fiber as a closed manifold L with π1(L) ≅ Z^k makes the question stand alone.
The quantifier should be sharpened from "close" to "sufficiently close".

The topology of closeness is not specified in Question 4.1 itself; nearby Question 4.2 discusses foliations that are C^1-close, so a stand-alone restatement should either fix a topology or explicitly note that the original formulation leaves this implicit.
The phrase "close to a fiber" should be clarified as meaning that the compact leaf of the perturbed foliation lies in a neighborhood of some fiber of the original fibration.
The surrounding discussion shows that the intended hypotheses are expected to depend on the monodromy of the fibration; that motivation is implicit in the draft but not stated.
refined_question: Let π:M→B be a fibration over a closed manifold B with closed fiber L satisfying π1(L) ≅ Z^k, and let F be the foliation of M whose leaves are the fibers of π. What hypotheses on this fibration, in particular on its monodromy, guarantee the following persistence property: every foliation G sufficiently close to F has a compact leaf contained in a neighborhood of some fiber of π?
justification: The draft is almost a verbatim restatement of Question 4.1, so that is the nearest official target in the paper. The surrounding text in Section 4.1 explains that the problem is motivated by the search for an index theory for compact leaves, analogous to the Poincare-Hopf or Fuller index, and it immediately adds that the known case B = S^1 depends on the monodromy. The paper then presents Question 4.2 as the next concrete specialization (torus fibrations over a genus-2 surface) and further reformulates that special case via monodromy and equivariant commuting vector fields in Questions 4.3 and 4.4. Those later questions sharpen the intended mechanism, but they are narrower than your draft. So the correct paper-faithful refinement is the general Question 4.1, with the monodromy emphasis made explicit from the nearby context.

citations.label: discussion following Question 4.1 (known case B = S^1; dependence on monodromy; BF94)
